files.purpose: This is the static HTML for the Droppy Code marketing home page (getdroppycode.app/), the dark sibling of getdroppy.app per the file's own top comment (lines 1-11): a fixed notch nav, a hero with a Hydra promo film, a 'One chat, many heads' section, a swipeable highlights carousel of seven feature cards, a 'bring your own agent' grid of twelve provider marks (Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, Antigravity, Copilot, DeepSeek, Command Code, Pi, Meta, Z.ai), a usage-limits popover showcase, a pinned wordscroll section for the 26 themes, a features tile grid, a 'Built for the Mac' stats/left-out block, a free/open-source download section, a ten-item FAQ accordion, an outro CTA and a five-column footer. Every screenshot and film embedded (tour/v5/*.webp) is captured from the real app in capture mode per the header comment, not hand-drawn, and the whole page has no build step -- it is served as-is with shared assets/css and assets/js.
key_symbols: section ids: hero, hydra, highlights, agents, usage, themes, features, mac, download, faq
#apple-mark shared inline <symbol> used by every 'for macOS' pill
data-binary-field / data-progress / data-scroll-span / data-density (hero and outro canvas particle fields)
data-highlight-carousel / data-highlight-rail / data-highlight-slide / data-highlight-prev / data-highlight-next (the 7-slide feature-highlights carousel)
data-wordscroll / data-wordscroll-glow / data-wordsplit (the pinned 'Make it yours' wordscroll section)
data-theme-picker (mount point the JS fills with the 26 theme swatches)
data-morph-glyph (arrow-glyph morph hint on pill buttons/links)
JSON-LD application/ld+json SoftwareApplication block (lines 64-78): name, operatingSystem macOS 26, offers price 0 EUR, sameAs the GitLab repo
calls_into: assets/css/site.css?v=14 and assets/css/wordscroll.css?v=5 (not read in this bundle)
assets/js/site.js?v=5, assets/js/wordscroll.js?v=5 and assets/js/code.js?v=7, all deferred (not read in this bundle)
https://fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com (Instrument Sans, Inter, Inter Tight)
https://droppy-releases.jordylegrand.workers.dev/site-assets/droppy-code/tour/v5/*.webp and .../usage/v1/limits.webp (remote-hosted app-capture media, R2-backed per the header comment)
side_effects: Inline <script> in <head> (line 55) reads/writes sessionStorage key 'droppyCodeNavIntro' in a try/catch, to skip the nav-intro reveal animation on a repeat view in the same tab -- identical snippet to website/changelog.html's.
platform_assumptions: Marketing copy throughout is macOS/Apple-silicon specific: 'Supercharged coding agent for Mac', 'native Liquid Glass window', 'Written entirely in Swift and SwiftUI ... for Apple silicon on macOS 26 and later. No web view, no Electron', Apple-mark SVG on every download pill, and the FAQ's 'Which Mac do I need?' / 'Which Mac' answers -- all describing the original macOS product and its own website, not the Windows app's UI.
The JSON-LD schema literally declares "operatingSystem": "macOS 26" and links the GitLab AGPL license and repo.
persisted_fields: sessionStorage['droppyCodeNavIntro'] (browser tab-local, marketing site only, not app data)
ui_elements: Fixed nav pill: logo+wordmark (Droppy Code), four in-page links (Hydra/Features/Changelog/FAQ), a menu toggle button, a Download CTA
Hero: 'The coding app by Droppy' kicker link, animated 'Supercharged coding agent for Mac' H1 with a charge/sheen effect, subtitle, Download + 'See what it does' actions, and the hero film image
Hydra section: heading/subtitle plus four tiles (full-width 'Meet Hydra' film, half-width 'pair a strong lead with quick heads', half-width 'Effort, fused' slider, full-width 'Panels that snap')
Highlights rail: a 7-slide ARIA carousel (Questions/Follow-ups/Changes/Command palette/Recipes/Intro/Threads) with prev/next arrow buttons
Agents grid: 12 provider entries, each an inline brand-color SVG mark plus a name label, under 'Bring your own agent'
Usage section: copy list (Plan limits/Credits/Lead and heads/Every account at once/Or keep it open) beside a usage popover screenshot
Wordscroll 'themes' section: bit-field decoration, wordsplit copy lines, and a data-theme-picker mount for the live theme swatches

Features tile grid: effort slider, model switcher, a tall sidebar art tile, a three-icon git trio (worktrees/commit-push-PR/project scripts), a first-launch tour tile, and six half-width fade tiles (Plans and to-dos, Notifications, Slash commands, Reply quotes, Panels, Bundled follow-ups) plus a themes film tile

'Built for the Mac' section: 5 stat tiles (100% Swift/SwiftUI, 10 agent providers, 26 themes, 1 dependency SwiftTerm, 0 telemetry) and a 'Left out on purpose' list (no remote access/mobile apps/cloud sync/telemetry/web client)
Download section: 'No price' heading, a free-app card showing 'Version 1.5.3 - Signed and notarized', a requirements checklist, Download / View source on GitLab / Join the Discord buttons

FAQ: 10 expand/collapse items (What is Droppy Code / Is it really free / open source / Do I need an API key / Which Mac / Does it send anything anywhere / How is this related to Droppy / checkpoints and worktrees / What is Hydra / usage limits / Where do I get help)
Outro: icon, heading, subtitle, Download + Discord + 'Meet Droppy for Mac' actions over a particle field

Footer: brand block (logo, tagline, description, Download CTA, live-year copyright, byline photo+name, 'made by Droppy' line) and four link columns (Menu, Droppy, Open source, Connect) plus a background wordmark
feature_notes: The entire B2->B3 diff (git diff 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc HEAD -- website/index.html) is a 6-line/3-pair cache-bust, identical in kind to website/changelog.html's: the query suffix on the shared OG image URL (https://getdroppycode.app/assets/og/og-home.png) changed from '?v=2' to '?v=3' in the three places it appears -- <meta property="og:image">, <meta property="og:image:secure_url"> and <meta name="twitter:image"> -- with every alt-text and every other line byte-identical to B2. Line count is unchanged at 782.
og-home.png itself is not part of this bundle's file list, so whether its pixel content actually changed for the 1.7.0 marketing cycle was not inspected here.

Source-fact oddity carried over unchanged from B2 (not part of this diff, but worth recording): the 'Built for the Mac' stats block says '10 agent providers' (line 510) while the agents grid immediately above it (lines 296-343) lists 12 provider marks (Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, Antigravity, Copilot, DeepSeek, Command Code, Pi, Meta, Z.ai). This is a pre-existing inconsistency in the marketing copy itself, not something introduced by B3, and has no bearing on the app's own provider list or parity records.

Also unchanged from B2: the free/download card's small print still reads 'Version 1.5.3 - Signed and notarized' (line 543), a stale marketing-site version string unrelated to both the B2 app version (1.6.2) and this B3 baseline (1.7.0); it is website copy, not app metadata, and outside this bundle's diff.

This file is classified 'first_party_website' / 'not_in_app_target' in porting/source_inventory.json (line 10526 entry), the same as website/changelog.html: required reading under CLAUDE.md's mandatory-reading list and PORT_CONTRACT.md:71 ('Read relevant documentation and the code of website components that supply app assets or runtime content; do not turn this into a website rewrite'), but never compiled into or shipped with the Windows app.

No porting/spec/*.json requirement/UI record cites this file (grep -n "website/index.html" over porting/spec/*.json returns nothing); the only incidental 'index.html' and 'website' string hits in that tree are unrelated -- MarkdownView.swift's linkifier example list and UPDATE.json's discussion of the app's own --website-captures launch-argument dead code (ED-061) -- neither is this marketing page.

porting/deps/units.json has no unit whose swift/target fields reference website/index.html, and no unit's spec field discusses the marketing home page; the Hydra/agents/usage/themes descriptions on this page are marketing paraphrase of app behavior that is independently specified (with its own source evidence) in HYDRA.json, PROVREG.json, USAGE.json and THEME.json respectively -- this page is not itself the evidence trail for those records.
unresolved_questions: Whether og-home.png's pixel content changed alongside its cache-busting version bump was not checked here and would need its own binary-asset bundle; it has no bearing on the Windows port either way since this whole file is out of the app build target.
